identity.mission: Read all XML configuration templates and Figma design markdown files, and execute a full end-to-end frontend implementation pipeline through to completion with complete one-shot execution.

technologies.item: Bootstrap 5 (Layout grid, responsive breakpoints, flexbox, utility classes)
Custom CSS (Scoped styling, CSS variables, typography, custom animations, media queries)

step.name: Figma Extraction Compilation
step.action: Read and parse all .txt extraction files in figma-extraction/ and compile them into structured .md design payloads inside compiled-payloads/ with their respective file names (e.g., figma-extraction/hero-section.txt -> compiled-payloads/compile-hero.md).

step.name: Reference Code & Payload Ingestion
step.action: Read all compiled .md files in compiled-payloads/, inspect design tokens and layout hierarchies, and cross-reference architecture and patterns from reference/index.html and reference/style.css.

step.name: One-Shot Code Execution
step.action: Implement complete, production-ready HTML markup into index.html and comprehensive custom styling into css/style.css without placeholders, omissions, or partial snippets.

step.name: Responsive Breakpoint Adaptation
step.action: Make project fully responsive for media query breakpoints of 980px, 757px, 575px, and 320px following strict priority order: Priority 1 (Bootstrap breakpoint utility classes such as sm, md, lg), Priority 2 (Bootstrap grid system using row, col, row-cols), and Priority 3 (Custom media queries in css/style.css ordered largest to smallest: 980px -> 757px -> 575px -> 320px, using a desktop-down approach rather than mobile-first).

step.name: Design & Reference Update
step.action: Continuously align and update implementations to match all Figma design tokens, extracted specifications, typography, colors, and layout hierarchies.

step.name: Human-in-the-Loop (HIL) Alignment
step.action: Provide direct output, pausing for human review and feedback at critical milestones without conversational noise.

guidelines_and_constraints.guideline: Execute complete one-shot implementations—avoid partial snippets, placeholders, or TODO comments.
Eliminate unnecessary conversation, filler text, and redundant conversational summaries.
Ensure exact alignment with Figma specifications and reference codebase standards.
Maintain full responsiveness across mobile, tablet, laptop, and desktop viewports.

Implement responsiveness across media query breakpoints (980px, 757px, 575px, 320px) adhering strictly to: Priority 1 (Bootstrap's breakpoint utility classes such as sm, md, lg), Priority 2 (Grid system: row, col, row-cols), and Priority 3 (Custom media queries in css/style.css applied desktop-down from largest to smallest: 980px, 757px, 575px, 320px; not mobile-first).
Properly reference assets using relative paths pointing to assets/images/.

Never hallucinate CSS classes, states, attributes, or content that do not explicitly exist in the Figma extraction .txt files. Every class name, state (e.g., active, hover, disabled), and text content in the output must have a direct, traceable origin in the Figma extraction source files.

The reference/ codebase is strictly an architectural and structural pattern source—use it only for layout patterns, component structure, and Bootstrap integration approaches. Never copy or derive class names, state classes, content, colors, typography values, or design tokens from reference/ files into the implementation. The Figma extraction files in figma-extraction/ are the sole source of truth for all design specifications.

css_rules.rule: Every element with a 'row' or 'row-cols-*' class MUST contain immediate children with 'col' or 'col-*' classes. Never place non-col elements directly inside a row.

First Priority: Always prioritize Bootstrap utility classes (including responsive breakpoint modifiers such as sm, md, lg) for layout, flexbox, grid, spacing (margin/padding), alignment, and responsive display.
Second Priority: Use Bootstrap grid system hierarchy (row, col, col-*, row-cols-*, row-cols-* responsive variants).

Third Priority: Use custom media queries in css/style.css for overrides and fine-tuning only when Bootstrap classes and grid are insufficient. Order custom media queries desktop-down from largest to smallest (980px, 757px, 575px, 320px)—NOT a mobile-first approach.
Never write inline styles (style="" attributes) inside HTML under any circumstance.
All custom CSS must be strictly written in the external stylesheet (css/style.css).
